Prev biopsy finding is left lobe, MRI finding highly suspicious of ISUP≥2 on right side. Active surveillance, only 1 biopsy session performed (of unclear date and unclear number of needles, unclear if targeted or systematic).

Young patient with high risk disease, should be recommended curative treatment. Biopsy report congruent with MRI, probably caught the index cancer at diagnosis. Highrisk flags are Gleason 5 pattern, cribriform pattern. Rather than new biopsy, consider low threshold for reevaluate MRI (T3-disease?, SVI?, nodes?) and possibly PSMA-PET for metastasis evaluation. Assess comorbidity closely.

Active surveillance of unfavorable intermediate risk disease, no previous re-biopsy. Likely biopsied index lesion on MRI, but note small tumor extension on biopsy (4mm) as compared with MRI lesion size (16mm). If biopsy with higher risk disease, likely recommendation on curative treatment. Plan talk to address LUTS/IPSS. If not curative treatment, potentially BPH treatment. 74yrs old will affect treatment plan.

Prev benign biopsy + PIRADS 3 (=no significant lesion) + low PSA-density -> Low longterm risk of lethal prostate cancer. 2yr too short interval for next assessment. suggest new PSA in two years, potentially new MRI with biopsy if PIRADS≥4

Rising PSA + PIRADS≥4 (limited size lesion) gives high probability of undetected prostate cancer. Therefore re-biopsy indicated. However, prev benign biopsy carries low longterm risk of lethal prostate cancer so is no acute rush to perform biopsy if patient would like to wait one year. Low PSA density supports that waiting can be tolerated. Will however need new biopsy within a few years.
AS for Intermediate risk PC in younger patient with very large prostate and only one biopsy procedure before. Needs confirmatory biopsy.
80yr, low risk PC. Only biopsy if signs of high risk PC, no indication for active treatment otherwise. Biopsyfinding congruent with MRI finding is reassuring.
Young increases importance of longterm risk assessment. BPH, low PSAd, benign MRI, no family history increases confidence to avoid biopsy at this point.

Advocate for curative treatment while unfavorable intermediate risk pc in young patient without significant comorbidity. IF he is cautious toward curative treatment, repeat biopsy to exclude higher-risk disease.

young patient with pirads5= high probability of significant prostate cancer and only one prev biopsy, increasing PSA. indicated with one more confirmatory biopsy to exclude significant disease (and curative treatment at this point)

Young patient with elevated PSA (>10), elevated PSA density, PIRADS5 and ISUP GG2 disease -> low threshold for recommending curative treatment. IF patient does not want to go to curative treatment, low threshold for biopsy to exclude higher-risk disease.

stable MRi findings in 70yr with reasonably low PSA. prev biopsy finding without obvious indication for treatment. IF patient want to be very active in treatment, consider biopsy and treat if higher-risk biopsy findings.
Highrisk disease in young patient. Should be treated, not get another biopsy.

Considering he chose not curative treatment at diagnosis, confirmatory biopsy is warranted to exclude higher risk disease. AS biopsy indicated after two years which seems to be now.
Younger patient, no reported comorbidity, high elevated PSA, high PSAdensity, PIRADS5, positive DRE. Clear indication biopsy.

Active surveillance, only one previous biopsy 2 yrs ago. Stable findings (stable PIRADS4, slightly increasing PSA) -> borderline indication for biopsy. As only one previous biopsy, would lean toward one confirmatory biopsy this time and potentially increase interval until next time. Alternative is to delay biopsy one year and do it then.

Borderline older patient, favorable intermediate risk disease with perineurial features. Low PSA (why was he biopsied in 2023 under non-elevated PSA?). While only one previous biopsy and intermediate risk disease, confirmatory biopsy after 2yrs recommended. Could potentially be postponed 1 yr.

Low risk PC with PSA <10. No red flags on biopsy or MRI, reasonably low PSA density. MRI finding minor and probably penetrated by systematic biopsy core (peripheral zone). Entered active surveillance this year, unclear to me how long time ago biopsy was. Slight recommendation new MRI two years with low threshold for biopsy then.

older patient with non-elevated, stable PSA. some comorbidity limits expected survival. MRI without significant lesions. Low risk of higher risk prostate cancer -> no biopsy. High risk of over diagnosis if biopsied.

This person should discuss curative treatment (younger patient with palpable, MRI-visible high-risk disease incl Gleason 5 findings). If not curative treatment for any reason, a strategy for medical treatment should be set. Potentially reasonable already now, but could also be delayed (but to the risk of disease progression).

74yr where it was decided to do MRI to assess potential PCa. The MRI shows high suspicion of PCa, and thus should be biopsied. Why was he not biopsied when the first MRI showed PIRADS5? (Ask about that reason before proceeding).

Intermediate risk disease in 75yr with some comorbidity. No targeted biopsy and unclear timing (when was diagnosis and prev biopsy). Unclear if PIRADS5 was biopsied (limited size lesion, unclear if new lesion while lack of previous MRI). Biopsy to exclude higher-risk disease, should include targeted cores.

Favourable risk intermediate risk PC in 73 yr old. Unclear when previous MRI+bx was performed. Reasonable to recommend another biopsy approx 2yrs after the first, especially if only 1 bx procedure before. Should probably only be treated if detected high-risk disease.
